summary: 63-year-old man with heart failure on spironolactone and 3 months of bilateral tender, rubbery, concentric subareolar discs. Gynaecomastia: medication review, examine the testes, endocrine bloods if no cause; no core biopsy for typical bilateral disease.

inputs.hpi: Three months of tender swelling behind both nipples, right slightly more than left. Heart failure diagnosed 6 months ago, started on spironolactone then. No nipple discharge. No weight loss. Drinks 10 units a week.

exam.general: Well. No stigmata of liver disease.
exam.other: Breasts: bilateral 3 cm rubbery, tender, concentric subareolar discs, mobile, no skin change or nipple retraction, no axillary nodes. Testes normal size, no masses.

comorbidities: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Bilateral gynaecomastia, probably spironolactone-induced
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Bilateral tender gynaecomastia, probably spironolactone-related. Discuss switching to eplerenone with cardiology; testes normal; LFT, TFT, testosterone, oestradiol, LH/FSH, hCG if persists.
